questions.explanation: Lemon is characterized by its sour taste; ice cream is characterized by its sweet taste. The remaining choices name a temperature, flavor, or ingredient rather than the corresponding taste.

questions.explanation: Gold can be made into a necklace; iron can be made into a bucket. Among the options, bucket is the matching object made from the named material.

questions.explanation: In the given pairs the second number is three-fifths of the first: 21/35 = 24/40 = 3/5. Thus (3/5)x = 36, so x = 60.

questions.question_text: Select the set related in the same way as (10, 20, 24, 16) and (18, 36, 40, 32).
questions.explanation: The successive operations are ×2, then +4, then −8: 10→20→24→16 and 18→36→40→32. Only 9→18→22→14 follows all three operations.
questions.source: Analogy 02_.pdf, lecture slide 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Choose the set related in the same way as (6, 12, 3) and (10, 20, 5).
questions.explanation: In each given triple, the second number is twice the first and the third is half the first. Only (14, 28, 7) satisfies both conditions.
questions.source: Analogy 02_.pdf, lecture slide 16; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Choose the set that follows the same successive operations as (1, 2, 4, 8) and (9, 10, 20, 40).
questions.explanation: The successive operations are +1, ×2, ×2. The first option gives 4→5→10→20, so it alone follows the same sequence of operations.
questions.source: Analogy 02_.pdf, lecture slide 27; exam/year not stated

questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure. The other quantities require different instruments.

questions.explanation: For n, the value is n³+n²+n: 4³+4²+4=84 and 13³+13²+13=2379. For 11 this is 1331+121+11=1463.

questions.explanation: The rule is n²−4: 6²−4=32 and 11²−4=117. Therefore 10²−4=96.
questions.source: Analogy 02_.pdf, lecture slide 19; exam/year not stated

questions.explanation: The output is the cube of one less than the input: (3−1)³=8 and (11−1)³=1000. Thus (6−1)³=125.

questions.explanation: Within each pair, the first letter advances by 2 and the second by 3: A→C, C→F. Applying those shifts gives M→O and O→R, hence OR.
questions.source: Analogy 02_.pdf, lecture slide 23; exam/year not stated

questions.explanation: The three letters are replaced by the letter whose alphabet position equals their sum: ABC gives 1+2+3=6 (F), BCD gives 2+3+4=9 (I), and CDE gives 3+4+5=12 (L). DEF gives 4+5+6=15 (O).
questions.source: Analogy 02_.pdf, lecture slide 24; exam/year not stated

questions.explanation: The rule is n³+n: 2³+2=10 and 4³+4=68. For 6, 6³+6=216+6=222.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.explanation: Apply increasing shifts of +1, +2, +3, and +4 to successive letters: ABCD becomes BDFH. Applying the same shifts to CDEF gives D, F, H, J: DFHJ.
